scene.speaker: astrid
scene.bubble: Everything in its place! My pencils here, my books there… and Pip on my chair. Again.
scene.intro: Astrid opens her school bag and puts everything in its place: this is her pen, this is her red pencil, this is her book, and this is her ruler. Everything is tidy — Astrid loves tidy things! But look at her chair… Pip is sleeping on it again, on top of the crayons. This is my chair, says Astrid. This is MY chair, says Pip. What is in YOUR school bag? Open it and say it in English!

words.clue: You write with it. Blue or black.
You read it. It has many pages.
You carry your things in it.
It is long. You draw lines with it.

activities.title: Match the thing with what you do.

data.script: Astrid: Look at my bag! Two books, three pencils and one ruler. … Nico: My bag has… one shoe? How did that get there? … Astrid: Nico! Where are your pencils? … Nico: Here! In my pocket. And my eraser is in my other pocket. … Astrid: My favourite thing is my red pen. It writes very well. … Nico: My favourite thing is my dinosaur crayon. It's green! … Astrid: School things ready. Let's go!

activities.title: Grammar · I have a book to read.
activities.instructions: Read the sentences. Then choose the right word.

data.title: I have a book to read.
data.intro: First say what you have. Then say what you do with it. One little word joins them: to.
data.can: I can say what I have and what I do with it: a book to read.

examples.text: Pip has a fish to eat. Look at him!

rules: have / has + a thing + to + do it.
The verb after to never changes: to read, to eat, to draw.
Now say one to your partner: "I have a ___ to ___."

items.sentence: She ___ a nice book to read.

outcomes.puede: Follow classroom instructions; identify familiar words in songs and short spoken sentences.
Greet; say name, age, colours; name objects; answer yes/no questions.
Recognise all 26 letters; match words to pictures (family, food, animals, body).
Write own name; trace and copy words; label pictures (3–5 words).
~150 productive words; Verb to be, can, like + noun, imperatives, this/that.
